answer: A protocol kernel binds each pseudo-identity to staking collateral, so dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and zero-knowledge verifiable delay make additional identities costlier than marginal utility. Subgame-perfect punishment matrices impose slashing penalties that grow with replicated attestations, creating a mesa where aggregate bond capital exceeds forgery gains. Thus the oasis of single honest key control yields negative expected Sybil attack utility, guaranteeing strict Nash equilibrium against adversarial multiplication.
